transcript.text: gas hob keeps clickin on its own since i cleand it, stops then starts agen. drivin me mad. pls help

That random clicking is almost always caused by moisture or debris on the spark electrode after cleaning. Please switch the hob off at the wall and unplug it (or isolate the fuse) for safety. If they look clean and dry but it still clicks, I'll need your hob's make and model number (usually on a sticker under the unit) to advise further.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok i unplugged it under the sink for the afternoon and its stopped clicking now. i dont know the model, its a bosch. no gas smell btw

That’s excellent news. The clicking stopping after you unplugged it suggests that moisture or cleaning residue on the spark electrode was causing the short circuit. To stop this happening again, just make sure all burner caps and crowns are completely dry before putting them back in place, and ensure they sit perfectly flat. If it starts doing it again despite being bone-dry, let me know.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

claimsRejected.claim: check the small white ceramic spark electrode near each burner to see if it's wet, dirty with food residue, or bent too close to the metal.
ensure all the burner caps are sitting perfectly flat and square.

candidates: Moisture or debris on the spark electrode (high)
Burner cap not seated correctly after cleaning (medium)

reading.symptom: keeps clicking on its own since cleaned it, stops then starts again

plan: They asked: "pls help" - answer that first.
Checks they have done and what they found: cleaned the hob - clicking started after cleaning.
The fault they reported is: "keeps clicking on its own since cleaned it, stops then starts again". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Say what that suggests, then ask for the make and model number so we can find the right part; say it is usually on the underside of the hob or on the guarantee card. If the label cannot be reached right now (for example the door will not open), say it can wait.
